newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer offers verbal support for dollar.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer offers verbal support for dollar.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer, in an apparent attempt to talk up the sagging dollar, said on Friday that U.S. economic fundamentals should allow the U.S. currency to be stronger.
"In my view the fundamental economic data in the United States would speak for the dollar to be valued at a slightly higher rate," Tietmeyer said.
The Bundesbank confirmed Tietmeyer's comments, made earlier to a German news agency, to Reuters on Friday in answer to an enquiry.
Tietmeyer's comments sent the dollar higher to trade near 1.4830 marks compared with 1.4805 marks.
The Bundesbank has long supported the idea of a slightly stronger dollar, saying a stronger mark would hurt the economy and would dampen Germany's exports.
Germany's fledgling economic recovery ground to a temporary halt last spring when the mark appreciated strongly against many European currencies and the dollar.
Only several weeks ago the Bundesbank took an unusual step in broadly hinting there could still be room to lower German interest rates at a time the dollar was falling under the 1.50 marks level.

However, After the Bundesbank disappointed markets by leaving interest rates unchanged in late July, the dollar suffered more weakness and international observers blamed the Bundesbank's inaction on rates.
A rate cut did emerge last Thursday when the Bundesbank again surprised markets by slashing the securities repurchase rate, repo, by 30 basis points to three percent.

Although the Bundesbank denies basing its monetary policy on currency rates, some analysts said the rate cut was partly motivated by expectations that lower interest rates would make German investments less attractive, weakening the mark.
